requirement: Continuation lines follow a documented line convention

obligations.note: Anchor line: obligation covers the whole assignment statement spanning lines 4-8. Lines 5-8 are continuation lines of this same statement and are deliberately NOT listed as separate obligations -- their absence here is the point, not an omission.

notes: This fixture's whole point is the line convention, not the arithmetic. Our chosen convention: a multi-line statement is one obligation, anchored to its first physical line (line 4). Lines 5-8 (a, + b, + c, )) are continuation lines of that same statement, not independent obligations -- under this project's oracle schema, a line not listed in any input's obligations is not a trackable obligation at all, which is exactly the right way to express 'these lines are not separate obligations' without a bespoke sentinel value. A provider that instead reports every physical line as hit (5, 6, 7, 8 each individually) is not wrong -- it uses a different, equally defensible convention -- but its result must be explicitly remapped to ours before comparison, never silently treated as a mismatch. This directly probes gd-tools 0.4.0's line-injection approach, since its plan generator walks a separately-parsed (gdtoolkit/Lark) syntax tree rather than the engine's own tree, and continuation lines are a plausible place for that second parser's line attribution to diverge from Godot's own executed-statement notion.
